title: The site writer can write its first draft in parallel parts (off by default): every page written once, merged and checked once, resumed, cancelled and costed per part, and a run that does not ask sends today's bytes
steps: S1: In the TCH checkout with dependencies installed and TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at a scratch Postgres, run run.cmd.
S2: Confirm every test named in run.tests reports ok.
expect: The split puts every page of the writing order in exactly one part, in order, with the heaviest part as light as any cut allows; the merged parts hold every slot of every page once and pass the copy check.

Each part's message starts with the same fixed part as a whole-site run, names its pages and the other parts' pages, the site voice, and shares out the business's own phrases and the phrases two parts' notes share.

A run started with parallel pages 2 sends both parts at the same time, saves them in separate turn ranges, checks one merged copy and costs the sum of its calls; the fix round continues the last part's conversation.

A run killed with one part recorded, or answered but not recorded, resumes the other part alone and never resends the first; a cancel stops both parts with no further call; a failed part stops the other and fails the run.

A run without parallel pages (or with 1) sends one request whose body is byte for byte the one sent before this change, and freezes no parallel setting; the CLI freezes --parallel-pages and refuses bad values and a mix with --pages-per-turn.

tests: the split puts every page in exactly one part
the merged parts are one copy with every slot of every page
each part gets the fixed part of a whole-site run
a phrase the notes of two parts share
off by default: the first message is the same bytes
a run without parallel pages sends one request
parallel pages: the parts are in flight at the same time
a fix round after parallel parts continues the last part
a part whose answer is not one JSON object is asked once more
a parallel draft killed after one part was recorded
a part answered but not yet recorded when the process died
a cancel stops every part in flight
a part that fails stops the other part
run --parallel-pages freezes the number of parts
